question.explanation:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the top equation by $10,$ as follows:

\[ \begin{cases} 0.2p=0.6 & \Big| \: \times 10 \\ -p-5q=7 & \end{cases} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} 2p = 6 \\ -p-5q=7 \end{cases} \]

Notice that we can easily solve for $p$ in the first equation:

\[ \begin{align*} 2p &= 6 \\[3pt] p &= 3 \end{align*} \]

Now, to find the value of $q,$ we can substitute $p=3$ into the second equation:

\[ \begin{align*} -p-5q &=7 \\[5pt] -3 -5q &= 7 \\[5pt] -5q &= 10 \\[5pt] q &= \dfrac{10}{-5} \\[5pt] q &= -2 \end{align*} \]

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $p=3, \,q=-2.$

question.explanation:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the top equation by $10,$ as follows: \[ \begin{cases} 3.6v+21.6=0 & \Big| \: \times 10 \\[5pt] 3v+4w+2=0 & \end{cases} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} 36v+216 = 0 \\[5pt] 3v+4w+2=0 \end{cases} \]

Notice that we can easily solve for $v$ in the first equation: \begin{align*} 36v+216 &= 0 \\[5pt] 36v &= -216 \\[5pt] v &= -6 \end{align*}

Now, to find the value of $w,$ we can substitute $v=-6$ into the second equation: \begin{align*} 3v+4w+2 &=0 \\[5pt] 3(-6) +4w +2 &= 0 \\[5pt] -18 +4w + 2 &= 0 \\[5pt] 4w &= 16 \\[3pt] w &= 4 \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $v=-6, \,w=4.$

example.title: Solving a System Containing Decimals in One Equation

question.text: Let $(a, b)$ be the solution of the following system. What is the value of $a+b?$ \[ \begin{cases} 0.05a-0.2b=0.04\\ 0.12a-1.2b=0.24 \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply both equations by $100,$ as follows:

\[ \begin{cases} 0.05a-0.2b=0.04 & {\Big| \times 100} \\[2pt] 0.12a-1.2b=0.24 & {\Big| \times 100} \end{cases} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} {5a-20b=4}\\[2pt] {12a-120b=24} \end{cases} \]

Notice that if we multiply the first equation by $-2$ and divide the second equation by $3,$ we will get a $40b$ term in the first equation that can cancel with the $-40b$ term in the second equation:

\[ \begin{cases} 5a-20b=4 & \Big| \: \times (-2) \\ 12a-120b=24 & \Big| \: \div 3 \end{cases} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} -10a+40b=-8 \\ 4a-40b=8 \end{cases} \]

Adding the two equations eliminates the $b$-variable and allows us to solve for $a\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \require{cancel} -10a+\cancel{40b}&=-8 \\ 4a-\cancel{40b}&=8 \\[3pt] \hline (-10a+4a)&= (-8+8)\\[3pt] -6a&=0 \\[3pt] a&=0 \end{align}

Finally, we can substitute $a=0$ into the equation $5a-20b=4$ to solve for $b\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 5a-20b&=4 \\[5pt] 5(0)-20b&=4 \\[5pt] -20b &= 4 \\[5pt] b &= -\dfrac{4}{20} \\[5pt] b &= -0.2 \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $a=0, \, b=-0.2.$ So,

\[ a+b=0+(-0.2)=-0.2.\]
